title: The if-else Statement
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the if-else statement and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—alternative execution paths—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study the if-else statement with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you make program paths and repetition predictable with explicit conditions and stopping rules. In this lesson, focus on alternative execution paths and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect alternative execution paths with multiple branches before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Multiple branches
items.text: Branches and loops define which statements execute and how often. State the branch conditions explicitly, make loop termination measurable, and test zero, one, and multiple-iteration cases. Apply that reasoning specifically to multiple branches and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: build the smallest program that demonstrates alternative execution paths. Change one input, predict the result, and add one boundary or invalid case before considering the task complete.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
